VI.description: Create a LabVIEW class - optionally inheriting from another\2C optionally with private data fields - by calling the project provider's OWN VIs\3A Add Class.lvlib\3AAdd Class to Project (path).vi and Message Maker.lvlib\3AAdd Member Data to Private Data Control.vi. Every input is a string because a helper's controls are set as strings over VI Server\3B the two paths are converted on the diagram.\0A\0AWHY NI'S VIs AND NOT A BUILT FILE. A class private data control is COMPILER OUTPUT\3A its type space (VCTP\2C TM80\2C the TopLevel map) and its data-space offsets describe a control\2C not the VI an AIXML cluster produces. Converting a generated VI into one by flipping flags gives a class LabVIEW reports normally and refuses to compile - Front panel control contains a data type with a type definition - and every accessor built against it breaks with it. Measured repeatedly\3B docs/lvclass-creation.md section 2a has the layout that would have to be synthesised. LabVIEW does it correctly in about 350 ms\2C so it does it.\0A\0AThe FIELDS come from a carrier VI\3A NI's VI takes an array of front-panel CONTROL REFERENCES\2C and each control's name and type becomes a field. AIXML generates such a VI perfectly - that is the one part of this it is good at. Pass an empty carrier path for a class with no private data.\0A\0AThe PARENT IS OPENED FROM ITS PATH with {LV.Application} LVClass.Open (uid 56)\2C and needs no project membership at all. Probed 2026-08-28 against a project listing no classes\3A the class opened\2C and read back its own Name and Path.\0A\0AThis replaced a search through the ACTIVE PROJECT - Build Array\2C CLSUIP_GetAllClassesInProject.vi\2C a For Loop reading each class's Path\2C To Upper Case\2C Search 1D Array\2C Index Array - five nodes whose only job was to turn a path the caller already knew into a refnum. That route made the parent's PROJECT MEMBERSHIP a precondition\2C which is why the .lvproj entry had to be written and the project closed to allow writing it\2C and it failed whenever LabVIEW's copy of the project was missing the class - measured repeatedly\2C always as a child created with NO parent and no error at all.\0A\0ALVClass.Open's ERROR TERMINALS ARE DELIBERATELY UNWIRED. A root class passes an empty parent path\2C which makes the call fail\3B leaving it out of the error chain turns that failure into exactly what is wanted\2C an invalid refnum meaning 'no parent'. The guard is not lost\2C it moved\3A uid 57/58 test the refnum with Not A Number/Path/Refnum? and report 'parent opened' as a boolean\2C so a parent that was asked for and did not open is still caught. Close uid 56 - this reference is ours\2C unlike the project's own objects - but close it OUT OF THE ERROR CHAIN (uid 88\2C error in wired for ordering\2C error out left dangling). A root class has no parent to open\2C so uid 56 is legitimately invalid\2C and closing an invalid refnum answers Error 1055\3A wired into the chain that turns every root class into a failed run. Measured.\0A\0ANEW CLASS OWNER STAYS UNWIRED (uid 62\2C an empty refnum)\2C so the class is NOT added to the .lvproj and the caller writes that entry itself after closing the project. That is a JUDGEMENT UNDER UNCERTAINTY\2C not a technical necessity\2C and the reasoning is worth keeping.\0A\0AThe owner IS reachable\3A {LV.Application} -> Project\3AActive Project -> {LV.Project} -> Targets -> Index Array [0] is My Computer. Spell it Targets\2C NOT Targets[]\2C which answers Property Node\3A Invalid property. Wired in\2C NI's provider lists the class in the live project itself and LabVIEW writes the .lvproj entry on its next save - confirmed repeatedly by projectEntry reporting alreadyListed instead of added. If it is ever wired again\2C do NOT close uid 26\3A the Class refnum at uid 89 is one the provider CREATED and must be released\2C but the target item is the live project's own object read out of a property.\0A\0AWHY IT IS NOT IN\2C measured 2026-08-28 over nine two-class runs (parent then child in one LabVIEW session)\3A unwired\2C 1 wedge in 4\3B wired\2C 3 wedges in 5. A wedge is LabVIEW hanging or its gRPC service going silent - always on the SECOND class\2C never with a wrong result\2C the classes themselves always correct. So the instability is not caused by the wiring - it happens unwired too - but the wiring is not shown to be harmless either\2C and the small sample points the wrong way. Two earlier explanations were tested and refuted\3A that closing the project caused it (three open/close cycles are clean)\2C and that a freshly regenerated helper caused it (a wedge happened with a cached one). The cause is OPEN.\0A\0ACLOSE THE CLASS REFERENCE\2C uid 89 - this is not tidiness. Add Class to Project (path).vi returns a Class refnum\2C and leaving it open KEEPS THE NEW CLASS IN LABVIEW'S MEMORY after the project is closed. The next run then opens a project that lists that class\2C LabVIEW will not bind the item to the copy already in memory\2C CLSUIP_GetAllClassesInProject.vi does not report it\2C and a child is created with NO PARENT and no error at all. Measured 2026-08-28 on a controlled pair\3A with the reference leaked\2C a parent and its child created back to back gave parent index -1 and only a LabVIEW RESTART cleared it\3B with this one Close Reference added\2C the same pair gave parent index 0 and a full two-class\2C twelve-accessor run needed no restart anywhere. The same leak is why a deleted .lvclass answers Error 1614 when it is created again.
